This document defines how data for the West Africa Micro Data 360 platform (AFW 360) are structured, coded and documented, how producers create data files, and how the database is extended to new countries, indicators and breakdowns. It follows the SDMX information model (the ISO standard statistical agencies use to exchange data) and borrows the World Bank Data360 dimension layout, stored as plain CSV files in git.

Background on the current inputs is in [input-tables-findings.qmd](input-tables-findings.qmd). Nothing here changes the legacy inputs under `data_raw/`. An R converter produces the new files from them ([transition.qmd](transition.qmd)), and the Python dashboard will switch over later.

**How to read this document.** @sec-idea is the whole idea on one page: the model, where every file lives, and how the database grows. Read it first. Sections [-@sec-data] to [-@sec-validation] are reference material; come back to them when you need the exact rule. @sec-decisions records the design decisions already taken and those still open. @tbl-reading-guide suggests where to start.

Every table in this document that lists the contents of a metadata file is generated from that file by `pipeline/build_docs.R` and included from `.docs/generated/` (@sec-generated-tables). Those tables cannot drift from the metadata; the prose around them can, and is what to fix if the two disagree.

| You are… | Read |
|---|---|
| A producer delivering a country's file | Sections [-@sec-idea], [-@sec-data] and [-@sec-deliver], then [-@sec-validation] to see what will be checked |
| Delivering a nowcast, projection or microsimulation | @sec-estimation-method, then the same sections as a producer |
| Adding a country, indicator, breakdown or qualifier | Sections [-@sec-growth] and [-@sec-extend], then the part of @sec-metadata that covers the codelist you are editing |
| Adding or changing a verification rule | Sections [-@sec-rules] and [-@sec-validation] |
| Writing the converter from the current Excel | Sections [-@sec-data] and [-@sec-metadata], and [Annex](#sec-appendix-legacy) |
| Writing the validator | Sections [-@sec-data], [-@sec-metadata], [-@sec-rules] and [-@sec-validation] |
| Working on the dashboard | Sections [-@sec-layout], [-@sec-cl-indicator] (display fields), [-@sec-reliability], [-@sec-assets] and [-@sec-text] |

: Where to start, by role {#tbl-reading-guide}

# The idea in one page {#sec-idea}

This standard exists so that every country's numbers arrive in the same shape. It is written for the country economists and data scientists who prepare indicators from household microdata, and it is what they work from when they add a country, an indicator or a new way of cutting the data. It is also the specification for the developers who build the converter, the validator and the dashboard on top of it.

The database it describes is meant to be a one-stop shop for country-level insight. Every indicator in it comes from national household microdata, and every number is stored the same way for every country.

## One row is one number {#sec-one-row}

Each row of a data file carries one value and the full set of codes that say what that value is: which country, which year, which population, which measure. Those codes fall into two families (@tbl-families), and telling them apart is the whole model.

|  | **Breakdown** | **Qualifier** |
|---|---|---|
| Answers | *Who* is counted | *What* is measured |
| Example | Rural households, Fatick, poorest quintile | At the \$4.20 line, in 2021 PPP, on disposable income, food category |
| Population behind each category | Different subsets of the same population | The same population every time |
| Test with `N_POP` | Categories **sum** to the parent | Each category **equals** the parent |
| Empty value means | `_T`: everyone, not split | `_Z`: does not apply |
| Declared in | `TAB_PLAN.csv`, per cut | `INDICATOR_QUALIFIERS.csv`, per indicator |
| Columns | `GEO`, `URBANISATION`, `SEX`, `AGE`, `COMP_BREAKDOWN_1…5` | `INDICATOR`, `MEASURE_QUAL_1…5` |

: The two families of codes {#tbl-families}

The quickest test is the population. If the people behind the categories add up to the whole, as regions or quintiles do, the variable is a breakdown. If every category covers the same whole population again, as the \$3.00 and \$4.20 poverty lines do, it is a qualifier. `N_POP`, the population behind each row, makes the test mechanical.

This matters for three reasons. The poverty rate at any line and PPP round is one indicator, `POV_HC`, not one per line. Every population share is one of three indicators — `POP_SH` (individuals), `POP_HH_SH` (households) or `POP_HE_SH` (enterprises), chosen by what the breakdown counts (D4) — not thirty. And a new grouping such as sector of employment is a row in a codelist, not a change to the file format.

The indicator, its qualifiers and, for a share, the category it is a share *of* together name a **series**: "poverty headcount at \$4.20 (2021 PPP)" or "share of employed persons working in agriculture". Every series is one row of `SERIES_PLAN.csv`, with a stable `series_id` and a display name, and every data row carries its `SERIES_ID` (D13). The series is what dashboards, reports and readers think in; the indicator and qualifier codes are how a series is built.

This distinction is the foundation of the database. Every rule in the rest of this document follows from it, and everyone who adds data has to apply it consistently.

## Common compositions, and how each number is checked {#sec-compositions}

@tbl-compositions builds some familiar numbers out of the two families. The last column shows what the coding buys in practice: once a number is coded this way, the validator can check it against related rows.

| The number you want | `INDICATOR` | Qualifiers: what is measured | Breakdowns: who is counted | How it is verified |
|---|---|---|---|-----------------------|
| Poverty rate at \$4.20 (2021 PPP) | `POV_HC` | `POVLINE_PL420`, `PPP_2021` | — | In 0–1; rises with the line, so `PL300 ≤ PL420 ≤ PL830` |
| …rural | `POV_HC` | `POVLINE_PL420`, `PPP_2021` | `URBANISATION=R` | `N_POP`-weighted average of `CAP`, `OU`, `R` equals the national value |
| …Fatick | `POV_HC` | `POVLINE_PL420`, `PPP_2021` | `GEO=SN03` | Same rule over all ADM1 units; their `N_POP` sums to the country |
| …at the national line | `POV_HC` | `POVLINE_NPL` | — | In 0–1; `PPP` not applicable |
| Number of poor people | `POV_NUM` | `POVLINE_PL420`, `PPP_2021` | — | Additive: sums across any breakdown; equals `POV_HC × N_POP` |
| Food share of consumption | `CONS_SH` | `COICOP_CP01` | — | **The 13 COICOP divisions sum to 1** |
| Housing share of consumption | `CONS_SH` | `COICOP_CP04` | — | Same closure; no separate "housing burden" indicator exists |
| Food share, poorest quintile | `CONS_SH` | `COICOP_CP01` | `QUINT_Q1` | Sums to 1 over COICOP within the quintile; Q1–Q5 aggregate to the total by `N_POP` |
| Food share among the poor at \$3.00 | `CONS_SH` | `POVLINE_PL300`, `PPP_2021`, `COICOP_CP01` | `POOR_Y` | `POOR_Y` and `POOR_N` aggregate to the total by `N_POP` |
| Share of employed working in agriculture | `POP_SH` | — | `EMP_SECTOR_AGR` | **Categories sum to 1** over the defining breakdown; the row's `N_POP` is the universe, employed persons (@sec-values) |
| Share of households with 2 enterprises | `POP_HH_SH` | — | `HE_COUNT_2` | Same rule; `HE_COUNT` describes households, so this is `POP_HH_SH`, not `POP_SH` (D4) |
| Gini of disposable income | `INEQ_GINI` | `WELFARE_INC_DISP` | — | In 0–1; `N_POP` equals the national population |
| Incidence of direct transfers, poorest decile | `FISC_INCIDENCE` | `WELFARE_INC_MARKET`, `FI_DIR_TRANSF` | `DEC_MKT_D01` | **Instruments sum to total incidence**; deciles aggregate by `N_POP` |
| Marginal contribution of indirect taxes to poverty | `FISC_MARG_CONTRIB` | `WELFARE_INC_CONSUMABLE`, `POVLINE_PL300`, `PPP_2021`, `FI_INDIR_TAX` | — | Instruments sum to the total effect |

: Common numbers composed from the two families, and how each is verified {#tbl-compositions}

Everything in the last column reduces to three generic rules, and `RULES.csv` says which of them apply to which indicator or series (@sec-rules):

1. **Aggregation.** Over a partition, totals sum, and means and shares aggregate as `N_POP`-weighted averages.
2. **Closure.** Some qualifiers partition the *measured quantity*: COICOP divisions sum to 1, and fiscal instruments sum to the total.
3. **Range and order.** Shares lie in 0–1, counts are non-negative, and the headcount rises with the poverty line.

@sec-example-rows shows these numbers as they are written in a data file.

## Where everything lives {#sec-layout}

Everything is plain files in one git repository, in ten top-level folders (@lst-layout):

- **`data_raw/`** holds the current legacy inputs, byte-frozen: file names and bytes unchanged, proven by `data_raw/CHECKSUMS.sha256` (D2).
- **`pipeline/`** holds the R code that reads `data_raw/` and the plans and writes every other folder: the metadata bootstrap, the converter, the validator and the SDMX generator and importer (D1, D11, D30).
- **`metadata/`** is the dictionary. It says what every code means, which rows a data file must contain, which rules the numbers must satisfy, and which surveys and program runs the numbers come from. Every other folder refers to it, and every change to it is reviewed (@sec-change-control).
- **`data/`** holds the numbers: one CSV per country, reference year and estimation method, each with a manifest recording how it was produced and against which metadata version.
- **`geo/`** holds the boundaries used for maps.
- **`content/`** and **`assets/`** hold the prose and images the dashboard shows beside the numbers.
- **`sdmx/`** holds the SDMX-ML structure message and the SDMX-CSV metadata messages, generated from `metadata/` and `content/`, committed and checked for staleness (D28, @sec-sdmx-generated).
- **`tools/`** holds tools outside the pipeline: the independent SDMX verification in Python (`tools/verify/`, D30) and the FMR install notes and scripts (`tools/fmr/`, D35).
- **`afw360/`** is the Python package of the dashboard loader, the one place the dashboard reads data from (D37).

Numbers flow one way. A producer's program computes indicators from the harmonized microdata and writes a data file and its manifest. The validator checks the file against `metadata/` (@sec-validation). The dashboard reads published files through a single loader. Until producers deliver files, the converter does their job: it turns the current Excel tables into data files using `LEGACY_LABELS.csv` ([Annex](#sec-appendix-legacy)).

**Metadata is generated once, then frozen (D11).** The first version of every file under `metadata/` was generated by an R script in `pipeline/bootstrap/`, from hand-written seed tables (`pipeline/bootstrap/seeds/*.csv`) and a small authored text file (`pipeline/bootstrap/text/*.csv`). From metadata version 0.1.0 onward, the CSV files under `metadata/` are the source of truth and are edited by hand through pull requests; the bootstrap scripts are frozen.

**Structural migrations are scripts, run once (D12).** When a release changes the columns of a metadata file or of the data file, the change is made by a script under `pipeline/migrations/<version>/`, committed with the release and run once. The script reads the previous version's files and writes the new ones, so the change is reviewable and reproducible; it never re-runs the bootstrap. After it has run, hand editing resumes.

The metadata, the converter and the validator exist, and the two countries' files have been produced from the legacy workbooks ([transition.qmd](transition.qmd)). The dashboard still reads `data_raw/` directly; the switch to the loader in `afw360/`, which reads `data/` (D37), is the remaining step.

## How the database grows {#sec-growth}

The rule for every extension is **metadata first, data last**. A number can enter the database only once its codes exist, so every change starts in the codelists and ends with a data file that the validator accepts. If a new number cannot be described with the existing codes, the codes are extended first, in the same pull request as the data.

**A new country** is added in this order:

1. Register the country in `CL_AREA`.
2. Register its spatial schemes in `CL_GEO_SCHEME` and their units in `CL_GEO`.
3. Check its indicators against the dictionary, `CL_INDICATOR`. Every country should produce the same set of indicators, matching the dictionary's codes, definitions and meaning. When a country's survey cannot match a definition, update the dictionary with a new code linked to the old one through `related`, rather than stretching an existing code to fit.
4. Do the same for breakdowns and qualifiers: the country's categories map to the shared codes in `CL_COMP_BREAKDOWN` and `CL_QUALIFIER`.
5. Describe the survey in `SURVEYS.csv`, and add the boundary files the maps need.
6. Produce the data file for each reference year, following `TAB_PLAN`, together with its manifest.

@sec-add-country gives each step in full.

**A new indicator** starts in the microdata, not in the aggregation. First standardize the variables it needs in the survey microdata itself, so that each one has the same definition, universe, unit and recall period in every country. Once they are standardized, the indicator is a simple aggregate of them: a mean, a share or a total over each cut. If an indicator needs complicated logic at the aggregation step, its variables are not yet standardized enough.

Every constructed variable also needs its own metadata, recording what the microdata looked like when the indicator was computed from it: the questionnaire module and questions, the recall period, the universe, the units and any recoding. `CL_INDICATOR` points to these variables through `source_questionnaire`, `source_vars` and `program`. Where the variable-level documentation itself is kept is still an open decision (@sec-open-decisions).

**Everything else**, such as a breakdown, a qualifier, a poverty line, a spatial scheme, a survey round, a piece of text or a figure, is listed in @tbl-extend with the files to edit and the version bump it needs. The only structural change is to the columns of the data file, and only the data team makes it (@sec-change-control).

# Data structure: dataflow `AFW360_HH` {#sec-data}

This section is the contract for the data file: its columns, what may go in each, and which rows it must contain. Read it before writing a producer program, the converter or the dashboard loader.

A *dataflow* is SDMX's name for a family of files that share one set of columns and codelists. `AFW360_HH` covers everything estimated from household-survey microdata: poverty, consumption, jobs, enterprises, agriculture, energy, housing, shocks, social protection, inequality and fiscal incidence. Fiscal incidence is *not* a separate dataflow. It comes from the same households and the same cuts, and differs only in its qualifiers.

A separate dataflow is needed only when the statistical unit is not the household population at all, for example tax parameters by bracket or macroeconomic series. The rule is: **a different statistical unit means a new dataflow; a new source, a new survey round or a model-based estimate means only a new file.** A nowcast or microsimulation of the same population is the same dataflow, told apart by the `ESTIMATION` dimension (@sec-estimation-method).

## Columns {#sec-columns}

Data files are SDMX-CSV 2.1 data messages (@sec-sdmx-csv) with exactly 37 columns, in this order (D46): the three fixed SDMX-CSV columns, then the 34 components of @tbl-columns in DSD order, which are 18 dimensions, `TIME_PERIOD`, nine measures and six attributes. The role says which family a component belongs to (@sec-one-row): breakdowns say who is counted, qualifiers say what is measured, the reference columns say how often, when and how the value was estimated, measures carry the value and its reliability, and attributes describe the value's identity, unit, status and origin.

{{< include generated/tbl-columns.md >}}

**Fixed columns.** SDMX-CSV requires them in every message. They are not components of the DSD and are not rows of `DSD_AFW360_HH.csv`.

- `STRUCTURE` is always `dataflow`.
- `STRUCTURE_ID` is `WB.AFW360:AFW360_HH(<VERSION>)`, with the content of `metadata/VERSION`: today `WB.AFW360:AFW360_HH(0.3.0)`.
- `ACTION` is `R` on every row (D38, @sec-values).

The `DATAFLOW` column of version 0.2.0 is gone: `STRUCTURE_ID` names the dataflow and its version.

**The key** is the 18 dimensions plus `TIME_PERIOD`, 19 columns, `FREQ` through `TIME_PERIOD`. Together they identify one observation, and no two rows of the database share them. `FREQ` is the first dimension and is always `A`, annual, coded by `CL_FREQ` (D34).

**Measures (D33).** An observation carries nine measures. `OBS_VALUE` is the value itself and is mandatory. `STD_ERR`, `CI_LOWER`, `CI_UPPER`, `N_OBS` and `N_POP` were attributes in version 0.2.0 and are now measures; their meaning is unchanged (@sec-values). Three optional measures are new: `N_OBS_NUM`, the unweighted number of records in the numerator of a share; `DEFF`, the design effect; and `DF`, the degrees of freedom of the variance estimate. None of the three can be derived from the others, and all matter for reliability. `N_OBS_NUM` is required where `STD_ERR` is; `DEFF` and `DF` are optional until a producer file defines them. Legacy files leave every measure but `OBS_VALUE` empty.

**Attributes.** Six attributes describe the observation. Each is attached at a stated level:

- `SERIES_ID` is attached to `INDICATOR` and the ten breakdown and qualifier dimensions, and `UNIT_MEASURE` to `REF_AREA` and `INDICATOR`. Both are repeated on every row and have exactly one value per combination of those dimensions across all data files; the validator checks this (`STRUCT.ATTR_LEVEL`, @sec-validation).
- `PRECISION`, `OBS_STATUS`, `SOURCE_ID` and `OBS_COMMENT` are attached to the observation. `OBS_STATUS` also relates to the measure `OBS_VALUE`.
- `SERIES_ID`, `UNIT_MEASURE`, `OBS_STATUS` and `SOURCE_ID` are mandatory and never empty (D39). `PRECISION` and `OBS_COMMENT` are optional.

Four of the attributes were added in version 0.2.0 so that a row can be read without opening any other file (D13 to D16):

- `SERIES_ID` names the series the row belongs to (@sec-series-plan). It is redundant with the key, and the validator checks that they agree. Its codelist `CL_SERIES` is derived from `SERIES_PLAN.csv` (D43).
- `UNIT_MEASURE` is the unit of `OBS_VALUE`, resolved for the country: `SHARE`, `PERSON`, `HA` or, for money, the ISO 4217 currency code such as `XOF` (@sec-values). All of them are codes of `CL_UNIT_MEASURE`, which was called `CL_UNIT` before version 0.3.0 and now lists the currency codes too (@sec-sdmx-global).
- `PRECISION` is the rounding unit of `OBS_VALUE` in base units, empty when the value is exact. A legacy conversion of a share rounded to two decimals writes `0.01`; a count converted from millions rounded to two decimals writes `10000`.
- `SOURCE_ID` names the program run that produced the row, in `SOURCES.csv` (@sec-sources). Its codelist `CL_SOURCE` is derived from that file (D43).

## The two sentinels {#sec-sentinels}

`_T` and `_Z` are reserved codes with fixed meanings. They are never listed in a codelist CSV, and no code in any codelist CSV may start with `_`. The SDMX generator adds them to the generated codelists, because SDMX validators accept only values that exist in the codelist (D42, @sec-code-rules).

- **`_T`, total.** The value covers every unit and is not split on this dimension. Valid in `GEO`, `SEX`, `AGE`, `URBANISATION` and the breakdown slots.
- **`_Z`, not applicable.** Valid in every unused qualifier slot, and in `SEX` or `AGE` when the indicator is not about individuals. A household-level indicator writes `SEX=_Z`, not `SEX=_T`, because "total over both sexes" would be a claim about a dimension that does not apply to households.
- `GEO` and `URBANISATION` are never `_Z`: every unit lives somewhere.

Three further SDMX sentinels are **reserved** and not yet used (D21): `_U` unknown, `_O` other, and `_X` not allocated. They exist so that a classification with a residual category can still be a partition that sums to one. No breakdown variable has such a category today; when one does, it uses these codes rather than inventing `OTHER` or `UNKNOWN` categories.

## Estimation method {#sec-estimation-method}

`ESTIMATION` is a key dimension that says how the value was produced (D17), with the codes of `CL_ESTIMATION`:

- **`SURVEY`**: a direct estimate from the survey microdata of the reference year.
- **`MODEL`**: a model-based value for the reference year, whether a nowcast, a projection or a microsimulation, built on an earlier survey or on scenario assumptions.

The two can coexist for the same country and year, for example a 2026 nowcast built on the 2021 survey next to the 2026 survey estimate once it exists. Because `ESTIMATION` is part of the key, the two never collide, and a chart can overlay them. They live in separate files, named `AFW360_HH_<ISO3>_<YEAR>_<ESTIMATION>.csv`, each with its own manifest and its own source in `SOURCES.csv`, which records the base survey and the program.

Every row of a `MODEL` file carries `OBS_STATUS=E` unless the cell is empty (`O`) or cannot exist (`M`). Which series a `MODEL` file must contain is declared in `SERIES_PLAN.csv`'s `estimation` column (@sec-series-plan); a nowcast typically covers poverty and inequality only.

## Rules for the breakdown columns {#sec-breakdown-rules}

1. **Fill the slots from the left, with no gaps.** Unused slots are `_T`.
2. **Use the canonical order.** When a row has several breakdowns, they go in ascending `slot_order` from `CL_BRK_VAR`, with ties broken alphabetically by `var_code`. Each combination then has exactly one spelling.
3. **One category per variable per row.**
4. **Respect unit compatibility.** A breakdown variable may be used only with indicators whose `stat_unit` appears in its `applies_to_units`.
5. **Never duplicate a named dimension.** Residence, individual sex, individual age and geography always go in their own columns.
6. **`SEX` and `AGE` describe the individual being counted**, not the household head. The head's characteristics are breakdown variables (`HHH_SEX`, `HHH_AGE`) and go in the slots.
7. **An age band that defines an indicator's universe is not a breakdown.** "Employed, 15–64" has that band in its `universe` and writes `AGE=_T`.

## Rules for the qualifier columns {#sec-qualifier-rules}

1. Fill from the left, with no gaps. Unused slots are `_Z`.
2. Use the canonical order: ascending `slot_order` from `CL_QUAL_VAR`, with ties broken alphabetically.
3. One category per qualifier variable per row.
4. **A row may use only the qualifiers its indicator declares** in `INDICATOR_QUALIFIERS.csv` (@sec-relations), plus any qualifier required by a breakdown it uses. `POOR_Y` requires a poverty line, so a food-share row broken down by poverty status carries `POVLINE_*` and `PPP_*` even though `CONS_SH` does not otherwise use them.
5. Pairings must be allowed: `QUALIFIER_PAIRS.csv` says which PPP rounds go with which line (@sec-relations).

## Values and attributes {#sec-values}

- **Store `OBS_VALUE` unrounded**, with `.` as the decimal separator and no thousands separator or `%` sign. Rounding is a display decision (`display_as`, `decimals`).
- **Use base units.** Shares are 0–1, never 0–100. People are counted in persons, not millions. Money is in whole currency units.
- **`UNIT_MEASURE`** repeats the indicator's `unit_measure` on every row, so the file can be read without the dictionary (D14). The dictionary stays country-neutral: a money indicator has `unit_measure = LCU` there, and the data row resolves it to the country's currency from `CL_AREA`, so a Senegal row says `XOF`. Every other unit is copied as is. The validator checks the two agree.
- **`PRECISION`** is empty for a value written unrounded, which is every value a producer delivers (D15). Only a conversion from an already-rounded source fills it, with the rounding unit in base units: `0.01` for a share rounded to two decimals, `10000` for a count that was published in millions with two decimals. The validator's tolerances and the dashboard's display cap read it (@sec-reliability).
- **`SOURCE_ID`** names the program run that produced the row, registered in `SOURCES.csv` (D16, @sec-sources). A file may hold rows from several sources, for example poverty from one program and fiscal incidence from another; the manifest lists them all.
- **Do not suppress.** Every estimate is published whatever its sample size. Reliability travels with the value instead: `N_OBS` and `N_POP` are required on every row, `STD_ERR` and the confidence interval on every row whose statistic admits them, and the dashboard shows them (@sec-reliability). A value that rests on too few records is flagged `OBS_STATUS=U`, not hidden (below).
- **`N_OBS`** is the unweighted number of **records of the estimation file** used: records in the group, in the indicator's universe, with a non-missing value. When a person-weighted poverty rate is computed on a household file, `N_OBS` counts households. `SURVEYS.analysis_units` records which file each `stat_unit` is estimated from, so a reader always knows what `N_OBS` counts.
- **`N_POP`** is the sum of weights over those same records: the population, households or enterprises the value refers to.
- **On a share row, both counts are the denominator** (D19). "Share of employed persons working in agriculture, poorest quintile" is estimated as a mean over employed persons in the quintile, and `N_OBS` and `N_POP` are the records and weighted population of that universe, not of the agricultural workers. The group is the population cut, quintile; the defining breakdown, sector, is what is measured. The agricultural workers' own population is `OBS_VALUE × N_POP` by definition, so it is not stored. The partition checks of @sec-validation therefore run over population cuts only, never over a series' defining breakdown.
- **Standard errors and confidence intervals** must reflect the survey design (weights, strata and PSUs, with linearized variance). Intervals are at 95%.
- **Rows from a legacy conversion** carry `PRECISION` and no reliability measures, because the workbooks hold neither. The exemption is a property of the source: the reliability columns are required on every row whose source has `kind = PRODUCER`, and may be empty where it has `kind = LEGACY_CONVERSION` (@sec-legacy).
- **Missing values (D39).** `OBS_VALUE` is `NaN` on every row whose `OBS_STATUS` is `O` or `M`, and a number on every other row. `NaN` is the SDMX-CSV value for an intentionally missing float or double; `#N/A`, the value for every other type, is not used. An optional measure or attribute that the source cannot supply is left empty, which SDMX-CSV reads as "not provided". The mandatory attributes `SERIES_ID`, `UNIT_MEASURE`, `OBS_STATUS` and `SOURCE_ID` are never empty.
- **`ACTION` is `R`** (replace) on every row of a published file (D38). `R` replaces whole observations and merges attributes above observation level; it does not delete observations missing from the file. A consumer that replaces a slice deletes it first, so a published file contains no `D` rows (@sec-sdmx-csv).

**`OBS_STATUS`** takes one of the codes in @tbl-obs-status, which come from the SDMX cross-domain `CL_OBS_STATUS`. A cell that can never exist is normally declared in the indicator's `excluded_breakdowns` (@sec-cl-indicator) and left out of the file. `M` covers such a cell when it has not been declared there: the row stays, with `OBS_VALUE = NaN`, so the gap is visible.

{{< include generated/tbl-obs-status.md >}}

Two of the codes are set by a rule rather than by judgement (D22):

- **`U`, low reliability**, applies when `N_OBS` is below the dataflow's minimum, or when the coefficient of variation `STD_ERR / |OBS_VALUE|` exceeds the dataflow's maximum for a statistic that admits a standard error. Both thresholds are rows of `RULES.csv` with scope `DATAFLOW` (`RELIABILITY_MIN_NOBS`, initially 30, and `RELIABILITY_MAX_CV`, initially 0.30). The producer writes the code, and the validator recomputes it and reports a mismatch as an error. A row with no `N_OBS` and no `STD_ERR`, as in a legacy conversion, is never `U`.
- **`D`, definition differs**, applies to every row of a series that a country produces with a definition that departs from the dictionary's. It is allowed only where `SERIES_PLAN.csv` has a row for that country and series with `status = DEVIATES` (@sec-series-plan), and is required on every row of such a series.

**One code per row.** When several apply, the first of `M`, `O`, `E`, `D`, `U`, `A` in that order is written. A model-based value that would also fail the reliability rule is therefore `E`, and its standard error stays visible for the reader's own judgement. `Q`, suppressed, is registered so that the code exists if a statistical office's confidentiality rule ever has to be honoured; nothing in the database uses it today, and the no-suppression policy stands.

## Which rows exist {#sec-required-rows}

`plans/SERIES_PLAN.csv` is the explicit list of series to produce: one row per `series_id`, naming its `ref_area`, `INDICATOR`, the qualifier combination in `MEASURE_QUALS` and, for a share indicator, the category it is a share of in `DEFINING_BREAKDOWN` (@sec-series-plan). A plain Cartesian product of qualifiers over cut categories over-generates — `CONS_SH` crossed with COICOP and poverty status gives 39 combinations where only 15 are real — so `SERIES_PLAN` states the real ones instead.

A series row with `ref_area = ALL` applies to every country. A row for a specific country **overrides** the `ALL` row for the same `series_id` and carries that country's `status`: `NOT_PRODUCED` when the survey cannot support the series, in which case no rows are required, or `DEVIATES` when the country produces it under a definition that departs from the dictionary's, in which case the rows are required and carry `OBS_STATUS=D` (D23). The `estimation` column says in which kind of file the series is expected, `SURVEY`, `MODEL` or both.

For each applicable `SERIES_PLAN` row whose `estimation` includes the file's `ESTIMATION` and whose status for the country is not `NOT_PRODUCED`, the required data rows are:

> (the cuts in `TAB_PLAN` compatible with the indicator's `stat_unit`, found through `CL_BRK_VAR.applies_to_units` rather than a unit column on `TAB_PLAN` itself — geography and urbanisation cuts apply to every unit) × (the categories of those cuts) − (anything listed in `excluded_breakdowns`) − (cells withheld in `LEGACY_OVERRIDES.csv`)

The coverage generator writes `SEX=_Z` and `AGE=_Z`, not `_T`, wherever `TAB_PLAN` says `sex = _T` / `age = _T` but the indicator's `stat_unit` is not `IND` (@sec-sentinels). It also keeps each generated row's provenance — its `cut_id` and defining breakdown — so that a check such as "the parent of a row" (@sec-validation) is computed from that provenance rather than guessed from the row's codes in general.

Nothing extra, nothing missing. A cell with no observations is a row with `OBS_STATUS=O`, not an absent row. This is what makes a file checkable: the validator can compute the set of rows that should exist and compare it with the rows that do.

A cell known to be wrong is different again: it is **withheld**, not published. Its row is absent from the file, the exclusion is registered in `metadata/plans/LEGACY_OVERRIDES.csv` (action `WITHHOLD`, with a reason and evidence), and the coverage check reads the register and subtracts it from the required rows (D5). Action `COMMENT` is not a withholding: the value is kept, `OBS_COMMENT` is set, and the row still counts as required.

: Example rows of a data file, showing only the columns that vary {#tbl-example-rows}

In every row `STRUCTURE=dataflow`, `STRUCTURE_ID=WB.AFW360:AFW360_HH(0.3.0)`, `ACTION=R`, `FREQ=A`, `REF_AREA=SEN`, `TIME_PERIOD=2021` and `ESTIMATION=SURVEY`. `SEX` and `AGE` are `_T` (total), or `_Z` for an indicator whose `stat_unit` is not `IND` (@sec-sentinels). `COMP_BREAKDOWN_2…5` are `_T`, and `MEASURE_QUAL_4…5` are `_Z` (not applicable). Each row also carries its `SERIES_ID`, for example `POV_HC.POVLINE_PL420.PPP_2021` on the first three rows and `POP_SH.EMP_SECTOR_AGR` on the agriculture row, its `UNIT_MEASURE` (`SHARE`, or `PERSON` for the number of poor) and its `SOURCE_ID`.

Qualifiers fill the slots in ascending `slot_order` (@sec-qualifier-rules): welfare concept 10, poverty line 20, PPP 30, COICOP 40, fiscal instrument 50. That is why the COICOP code lands in slot 3 on the "food share among the poor" row but in slot 1 on the "food share, poorest quintile" row.

# SDMX conformance {#sec-sdmx}

This section says how the database maps onto SDMX. The project targets the SDMX 3.1 family: SDMX-CSV 2.1.0 for data and reference metadata, and SDMX-ML 3.1.0 for structures (D27). No SDMX-JSON is produced (D29).

The CSV files under `metadata/`, `content/` and `data/` remain the source of truth. The SDMX-ML structure message and the SDMX-CSV metadata messages are generated from them, committed, and checked for staleness like the generated tables of this document (D28, D20). Nobody edits the XML by hand. The pipeline stays in R: R writes the XML and validates it against the SDMX-ML XSDs. Python is used only by the dashboard loader and by a separate verification tool that is never part of the pipeline (D30).

## Identity and versioning {#sec-sdmx-identity}

- **Agency.** Every artefact is maintained by `WB.AFW360`, a sub-agency of the registered World Bank agency `WB` (D31).
- **Agency scheme.** The project ships a `WB:AGENCIES` agency scheme (fixed id, no version attribute in XML) that declares one agency, `AFW360`, named "West Africa Micro Data 360 (AFW DIP/POV team)". It is a local placeholder so that `WB.AFW360` resolves in FMR, pysdmx and the XSD and URN checks. It asserts nothing in the World Bank's namespace and is never submitted to any registry. At registration it is replaced by the World Bank's own scheme. Before loading into a World Bank registry, check whether `WB:AGENCIES` already exists there; if it does, have `AFW360` added to it and drop the local copy. Global registration is a later step, taken by the World Bank's SDMX owner.
- **Version.** Every maintainable artefact carries `agencyID="WB.AFW360"` and `version="0.3.0"`, the content of `metadata/VERSION` (D40).
- **Semver dependency rule.** A semver artefact references only semver artefacts (IM technical notes, Annex "Semantic Versioning", "Dependency Management"; the XSD does not enforce it). The one exception is a reference to an item of the fixed-version organisation schemes, `AGENCIES`, `DATA_PROVIDERS` and `METADATA_PROVIDERS`, whose URN version is `(1.0)`. The XSD requires those references, and the `SDMX.URN` check exempts them. Annotation values such as `GLOBAL_CODE` and `SDMX_CROSS_DOMAIN_CONCEPT` are not structural references.
- **URN form.** `urn:sdmx:org.sdmx.infomodel.<package>.<Class>=WB.AFW360:<ID>(0.3.0)`. A code appends `.<CODE>`.
- **Short reference form**, used in CSV messages: `WB.AFW360:<ID>(0.3.0)`.
- **Message header sender id**: `WB_AFW360`. Sender ids are plain IDs and cannot contain a dot.
- **Artefact ids** are NCNames: a letter, then letters, digits, `_` or `-`. The project code rules (@sec-code-rules) are stricter and stay.
- **Released artefacts are immutable.** A released `X.Y.Z` never changes (SDMX semantic versioning). Edits between releases are made on a `-draft` copy and re-imported into the CSVs; the next release bumps `VERSION` and regenerates every artefact (D40, @sec-change-control).

## The data file as an SDMX-CSV message {#sec-sdmx-csv}

Every data file is an SDMX-CSV 2.1 data message. Here is the header and the first row of `data/AFW360_HH_SEN_2021_SURVEY.csv`. Each is one line in the file; they are shown wrapped here.

```
STRUCTURE,STRUCTURE_ID,ACTION,FREQ,REF_AREA,GEO,ESTIMATION,INDICATOR,SEX,AGE,URBANISATION,
COMP_BREAKDOWN_1,COMP_BREAKDOWN_2,COMP_BREAKDOWN_3,COMP_BREAKDOWN_4,COMP_BREAKDOWN_5,
MEASURE_QUAL_1,MEASURE_QUAL_2,MEASURE_QUAL_3,MEASURE_QUAL_4,MEASURE_QUAL_5,TIME_PERIOD,
OBS_VALUE,STD_ERR,CI_LOWER,CI_UPPER,N_OBS,N_POP,N_OBS_NUM,DEFF,DF,
SERIES_ID,UNIT_MEASURE,PRECISION,OBS_STATUS,SOURCE_ID,OBS_COMMENT
dataflow,WB.AFW360:AFW360_HH(0.3.0),R,A,SEN,SN01,SURVEY,AGR_CULTIVATES,_Z,_Z,_T,
_T,_T,_T,_T,_T,_Z,_Z,_Z,_Z,_Z,2021,
0.01,,,,,,,,,
AGR_CULTIVATES,SHARE,0.01,A,SEN_EHCVM2021_LEGACY_v1,
```

In this row `GEO = SN01` is the `CL_GEO` code of Dakar (ADM1). National totals use `GEO = _T`.

Rules:

- **37 columns, in DSD order (D46):** the three fixed columns, the 18 dimensions, `TIME_PERIOD`, the nine measures, then the six attributes. The key is the 18 dimensions plus `TIME_PERIOD`, 19 columns (@sec-columns). The header is one physical line.
- **`STRUCTURE`** is always `dataflow`. **`STRUCTURE_ID`** is `WB.AFW360:AFW360_HH(<VERSION>)`.
- **`ACTION` is `R`**, replace, in every published file (D38). The SDMX-CSV 2.1 guide recommends `R` for complete query responses; `I` and `A` are deprecated. `R` replaces whole observations and merges attributes above observation level. It does not delete observations missing from the file. A consumer that replaces a slice deletes it first, with a `D` row of the partial key `REF_AREA`, `ESTIMATION`, `TIME_PERIOD`. The published files contain no `D` rows.
- **`FREQ`** is `A`.
- **Missing values (D39).** `OBS_VALUE` is `NaN` when `OBS_STATUS` is `O` or `M`, and a number otherwise. `NaN` is the SDMX-CSV intentionally-missing value for float and double components only. `#N/A` is the value for every other type and is not used. Optional measures and optional attributes are left empty when not available; in SDMX-CSV, empty means "not provided". The mandatory attributes `SERIES_ID`, `UNIT_MEASURE`, `OBS_STATUS` and `SOURCE_ID` are never empty.
- **Attributes on partial keys.** `SERIES_ID` and `UNIT_MEASURE` are attached to partial keys, replicated on every row, and carry exactly one value per partial key across all data files: `SERIES_ID` per `INDICATOR` and the ten breakdown and qualifier dimensions, `UNIT_MEASURE` per `REF_AREA` and `INDICATOR`. The validator check `STRUCT.ATTR_LEVEL` (ERROR) groups all rows of all files by each attribute's relationship dimensions and reports any group with more than one distinct value.
- **Numbers** use `.` as the decimal separator and no thousands separator.
- **Encoding.** RFC 4180 quoting, written with `readr::write_csv(..., na = "")`, so readr's default `NA` never appears. UTF-8 without BOM, LF line endings. LF is a project convention and a documented deviation from RFC 4180, which specifies CRLF; the SDMX-CSV 2.1 guide does not address line endings or BOM.
- **File names** are unchanged: `AFW360_HH_<ISO3>_<YEAR>_<ESTIMATION>.csv`.
- **Manifest.** The key `dataflow` becomes `structure_id`, and a new key `sdmx_csv_version` holds `2.1.0` (@sec-manifest). The manifest stays a project-level sidecar; it describes a file, which is not an SDMX artefact.

## Data structure definition `DSD_AFW360_HH` {#sec-sdmx-dsd}

The dataflow `WB.AFW360:AFW360_HH(0.3.0)` references the data structure definition `WB.AFW360:DSD_AFW360_HH(0.3.0)`. Its components are the rows of `metadata/structure/DSD_AFW360_HH.csv`, listed in @tbl-columns, which is generated from that file and is authoritative. @tbl-sdmx-dsd summarises them in data-file order. The three fixed SDMX-CSV columns are not components and are not rows of the DSD file.

| Pos | Id | Component | Project role | Codelist | Data type | Usage | Relationship | Sentinel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `FREQ` | dimension | reference | `CL_FREQ` | | | | |
| 2 | `REF_AREA` | dimension | breakdown | `CL_AREA` | | | | |
| 3 | `GEO` | dimension | breakdown | `CL_GEO` | | | | `_T` |
| 4 | `ESTIMATION` | dimension | reference | `CL_ESTIMATION` | | | | |
| 5 | `INDICATOR` | dimension | qualifier | `CL_INDICATOR` | | | | |
| 6 | `SEX` | dimension | breakdown | `CL_SEX` | | | | `_T` `_Z` |
| 7 | `AGE` | dimension | breakdown | `CL_AGE` | | | | `_T` `_Z` |
| 8 | `URBANISATION` | dimension | breakdown | `CL_URBANISATION` | | | | `_T` |
| 9 to 13 | `COMP_BREAKDOWN_1..5` | dimension | breakdown | `CL_COMP_BREAKDOWN` | | | | `_T` |
| 14 to 18 | `MEASURE_QUAL_1..5` | dimension | qualifier | `CL_QUALIFIER` | | | | `_Z` |
| 19 | `TIME_PERIOD` | time_dimension | reference | | GregorianYear | | | |
| 20 | `OBS_VALUE` | measure | measure | | Double | mandatory | | |
| 21 | `STD_ERR` | measure | measure | | Double, min 0 | optional | | |
| 22 | `CI_LOWER` | measure | measure | | Double | optional | | |
| 23 | `CI_UPPER` | measure | measure | | Double | optional | | |
| 24 | `N_OBS` | measure | measure | | Integer, min 0 | optional | | |
| 25 | `N_POP` | measure | measure | | Double, min 0 | optional | | |
| 26 | `N_OBS_NUM` | measure | measure | | Integer, min 0 | optional | | |
| 27 | `DEFF` | measure | measure | | Double, min 0 | optional | | |
| 28 | `DF` | measure | measure | | Integer, min 0 | optional | | |
| 29 | `SERIES_ID` | attribute | attribute | `CL_SERIES` (derived) | | mandatory | dimensions: `INDICATOR` `COMP_BREAKDOWN_1..5` `MEASURE_QUAL_1..5` | |
| 30 | `UNIT_MEASURE` | attribute | attribute | `CL_UNIT_MEASURE` | | mandatory | dimensions: `REF_AREA` `INDICATOR` | |
| 31 | `PRECISION` | attribute | attribute | | Double, min 0 | optional | observation | |

| 34 | `OBS_COMMENT` | attribute | attribute | | String | optional | observation | |

: Components of `DSD_AFW360_HH`, in data-file order {#tbl-sdmx-dsd}

- **`Pos` is the CSV column order only.** In SDMX-ML the writer emits `DimensionList` (rows 1 to 19), then `AttributeList` (rows 29 to 34), then `MeasureList` (rows 20 to 28), as the XSD requires.
- **Usage and requiredness.** The project's requiredness (R, C, O) and its conditions are unchanged. For example, `STD_ERR` is required on rows of a `PRODUCER` source where the statistic admits it. They stay in the DSD file's `required` column and in the validator. SDMX `usage` is the weaker, structural statement. Of the three new measures, `N_OBS_NUM` is C with the same condition as `STD_ERR`, and `DEFF` and `DF` are O until a producer file defines them.
- **Concept identity.** Every component has a concept of the same id in `CS_AFW360` (@sec-sdmx-concepts).
- **Time.** The time dimension's representation is written explicitly, `TextFormat textType="GregorianYear"`.
- **No MSD link.** The DSD does not reference the metadata structure, because data-related reference metadata is not used.

## Codelists and the CSV-to-SDMX mapping {#sec-sdmx-mapping}

Every `metadata/codelists/CL_*.csv` becomes a codelist `WB.AFW360:CL_*(0.3.0)`. Columns map to SDMX by convention, with no mapping file to maintain (D41). The mapping is mechanical and reversible, which the FMR round-trip needs.

| CSV column | SDMX |
|---|---|
| `code` | `Code/@id` |
| `name_en` | `Name xml:lang="en"` |
| `definition_en` | `Description xml:lang="en"`, omitted when empty |
| `parent` | `Parent`, in the same codelist |
| `global_urn` | annotation type `GLOBAL_CODE`, value the URN |
| `status`, `version_added`, `replaced_by`, `notes` | annotations `AFW_STATUS`, `AFW_VERSION_ADDED`, `AFW_REPLACED_BY`, `AFW_NOTES` |
| any other column | annotation `AFW_<COLUMN>` (column name upper-cased), value the cell text as is; space-separated lists stay space-separated |

: How a codelist CSV maps to SDMX (D41) {#tbl-sdmx-mapping}

**The annotation registry.** An annotation is written as `Annotation id="<type>"`, with `AnnotationType` the type and `AnnotationValue` the value. Annotations are the first child of the code. An empty cell produces no annotation. The annotation types in use are:

- `GLOBAL_CODE`: the full code URN of the matching code in a global list (@sec-sdmx-global).
- `AFW_<COLUMN>`: one per codelist column that has no SDMX slot, including `AFW_STATUS`, `AFW_VERSION_ADDED`, `AFW_REPLACED_BY` and `AFW_NOTES`.
- `AFW_SENTINEL`: `Y` on a sentinel code added by the generator.
- `AFW_SOURCE_FILE` and `AFW_METADATA_VERSION`: on every maintainable artefact, the repository path of the CSV it was generated from and the metadata version.
- `SDMX_CROSS_DOMAIN_CONCEPT`: on a concept that matches an SDMX cross-domain concept (@sec-sdmx-concepts).

Special cases:

- **`CL_GEO_SCHEME.csv`** is keyed by `ref_area` and `code`. Its SDMX code id is `<ref_area>_<code>`, for example `SEN_ADM1`, and the two parts are also kept as annotations. The importer splits the id on the first underscore.
- **Sentinels (D42).** The generator appends `_T` ("Total") and `_Z` ("Not applicable") as real codes, reading the DSD file's `sentinel` column: `_T` to `CL_GEO`; `_T` and `_Z` to `CL_SEX` and `CL_AGE`; `_T` to `CL_URBANISATION` and `CL_COMP_BREAKDOWN`; `_Z` to `CL_QUALIFIER`. That is eight sentinel codes in all. Each carries `AFW_SENTINEL` = `Y`, which the importer uses to drop it again, and one `GLOBAL_CODE`. The `GLOBAL_CODE` is the matching code in the list's own global counterpart where one exists: `CL_SEX` `_T` and `_Z` point to `SDMX:CL_SEX(2.1)._T` and `._Z`, `CL_AGE._T` to `IAEG-SDGs:CL_AGE(1.25)._T`, `CL_URBANISATION._T` to `IAEG-SDGs:CL_URBANISATION(1.10)._T`, and `CL_COMP_BREAKDOWN._T` to `IAEG-SDGs:CL_QUANTILE(1.1)._T`. Where the own list has no such code (`CL_AGE._Z`, `CL_GEO._T`, `CL_QUALIFIER._Z`), the value is `SDMX:CL_SEX(2.1)._T` or `._Z`. All of these are written as full code URNs. The sentinels still never appear in the codelist CSVs (@sec-code-rules).
- **Full URNs.** `GLOBAL_CODE` and `global_urn` values are always full code URNs, `urn:sdmx:org.sdmx.infomodel.codelist.Code=<agency>:<id>(<version>).<code>`, never the short form.
- **Derived codelists (D43).** Four registries become codelists. `CL_SERIES` comes from `plans/SERIES_PLAN.csv`, one code per distinct `series_id`, named by the `name_en` of the `ALL` row, with `AFW_STATUS` from the `ALL` row. `CL_SOURCE` comes from `registries/SOURCES.csv`, named by `source_id`, described by `notes`. `CL_SURVEY` comes from `surveys/SURVEYS.csv`, named by `survey_name`. `CL_FIGURE` comes from `registries/FIGURES.csv`, named by `title_en`. Derived codelists carry only id, name, description and `AFW_STATUS`; every other column goes to a metadataset (@sec-sdmx-refmeta). This gives `SERIES_ID` and `SOURCE_ID` real codelists.
- **Names and descriptions of artefacts** come from `metadata/structure/ARTEFACTS.csv` (D44). It lists every SDMX artefact to generate, one row each, with `artefact_id`, `artefact_type` (the SDMX class name), `agency_id`, `source_file`, `name_en`, `description_en`, `status`, `version_added` and `notes`. The generator iterates over it, so the list of what to generate is data, not code.

## Concepts {#sec-sdmx-concepts}

The concept scheme `CS_AFW360` has one concept per component id of @tbl-sdmx-dsd, from `FREQ` to `OBS_COMMENT`. The five `COMP_BREAKDOWN_n` and the five `MEASURE_QUAL_n` are separate concepts. It also has one concept per metadata attribute of the MSD (@sec-sdmx-refmeta).

- A component's concept takes its name and description from the DSD file (`name_en`, `description`). A metadata attribute's concept takes them from `COLUMNS.csv`: the `column` humanised as the name, and `description` as the description.
- A concept that matches an SDMX cross-domain concept carries the annotation `SDMX_CROSS_DOMAIN_CONCEPT`, with the concept id in `SDMX:CROSS_DOMAIN_CONCEPTS(2.0)`: `FREQ`, `REF_AREA`, `TIME_PERIOD`, `OBS_VALUE`, `OBS_STATUS`, `UNIT_MEASURE`, `SEX`, `AGE`, `INDICATOR`, `OBS_COMMENT` (to `COMMENT`) and `SOURCE_ID` (to `DATA_SOURCE`).
- Core representation: a coded concept references its codelist; a numeric one carries the `TextFormat` of @tbl-sdmx-dsd; a text one is `String`. `TIME_PERIOD` carries `TextFormat textType="GregorianYear"`, the same as its time-dimension local representation.

## Reference metadata {#sec-sdmx-refmeta}

Documentary metadata goes where SDMX puts it: in metadatasets of a metadata structure (D43).

- **MSD `WB.AFW360:MSD_AFW360(0.3.0)`** has four presentational parent attributes, `SURVEY`, `SOURCE`, `TEXT` and `FIGURE`. Each parent is `isPresentational="true"`, `minOccurs="0"`, `maxOccurs="1"`, with no `LocalRepresentation`, because the XSD default for `minOccurs` is 1 and each metadataset fills only one parent. Each parent has one child per source column, minus the id and `status` columns, with ids equal to the column names upper-cased. Children have `TextFormat textType="String"`, `minOccurs="0"` and `maxOccurs="1"`.
  - `SURVEY`: `SURVEYS.csv` columns 2 to 24 (`REF_AREA`, `TIME_PERIOD`, `SURVEY_NAME`, ... `NOTES`).
  - `SOURCE`: `SOURCES.csv` columns 2 to 13.
  - `TEXT`: `SLOT`, `REF_AREA`, `TIME_PERIOD`, `ORDER`, `TITLE`, `BODY`, `UPDATED_ON`. `BODY` holds the Markdown source: the `body` cell, or the content of the `file` when set.
  - `FIGURE`: `FIGURES.csv` columns 2 to 16 (`REF_AREA` ... `NOTES`, excluding `figure_id` and `status`).
- **Metadataflow `MDF_AFW360`** has the structure `MSD_AFW360` and four explicit `Target` elements, one per targeted artefact: the codelists `CL_SURVEY`, `CL_SOURCE` and `CL_FIGURE`, and the dataflow `AFW360_HH`, each as a full URN with version `0.3.0`. Wildcard targets are schema-valid but not used. The generator rewrites the versions at each release, like every other reference.
- **Metadatasets**, one per registry row, are written as SDMX-CSV 2.1 metadata messages under `sdmx/metadata/`. The header is `MDSTRUCTURE,MDSTRUCTURE_ID,METADATASET_ID,TARGET_TYPES,TARGET_IDS`, then the attribute columns. `MDSTRUCTURE` is `metadataflow` and `MDSTRUCTURE_ID` is `WB.AFW360:MDF_AFW360(0.3.0)`. Presentational parents have no column; each child appears as `<PARENT>.<CHILD>`, for example `SURVEY.SURVEY_NAME`. Metadatasets are not versioned.
- **Targets are whole artefacts**, as the SDMX-CSV 2.1 metadata guide defines them: `TARGET_TYPES` is a REST structure resource name and `TARGET_IDS` is `AGENCY:ID(VERSION)`. The guide has no form that targets a single code. The item a metadataset describes is identified by its `METADATASET_ID` and by the key attributes inside it, such as `SURVEY.REF_AREA` and `SURVEY.TIME_PERIOD`. `TEXT.csv` rows are metadatasets about a country; they target the dataflow and name the country in `TEXT.REF_AREA`.

| File | `METADATASET_ID` | `TARGET_TYPES` | `TARGET_IDS` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MDS_SURVEYS.csv` | `WB.AFW360:MDS_SURVEY_<survey_id>` | `codelist` | `WB.AFW360:CL_SURVEY(0.3.0)` |
| `MDS_SOURCES.csv` | `WB.AFW360:MDS_SOURCE_<source_id>` | `codelist` | `WB.AFW360:CL_SOURCE(0.3.0)` |
| `MDS_TEXT.csv` | `WB.AFW360:MDS_TEXT_<slot>_<ref_area>_<time_period>_<order>` | `dataflow` | `WB.AFW360:AFW360_HH(0.3.0)` |
| `MDS_FIGURES.csv` | `WB.AFW360:MDS_FIGURE_<figure_id>` | `codelist` | `WB.AFW360:CL_FIGURE(0.3.0)` |

: SDMX-CSV metadata messages (D43) {#tbl-sdmx-metadatasets}

The metadata files are written with `readr::write_csv(quote = "all", na = "")`, because the guide recommends quoting every textual value and every MSD attribute is `String`. pysdmx 1.20.0 has no SDMX-CSV metadata reader, so the independent check of these files is a header check in `tools/verify/`; FMR is the second reader when installed.

## Providers {#sec-sdmx-providers}

- `DataProviderScheme` `DATA_PROVIDERS` (agency `WB.AFW360`, fixed version) has one provider, `AFW_POV` ("AFW DIP/POV team"). The `ProvisionAgreement` `PA_AFW360_HH` links the dataflow and the provider.
- `MetadataProviderScheme` `METADATA_PROVIDERS` (agency `WB.AFW360`) has the provider `AFW_POV`. The `MetadataProvisionAgreement` `MPA_AFW360` links the metadataflow and the provider.
- The agreements reference `DATA_PROVIDERS(1.0)` and `METADATA_PROVIDERS(1.0)`, the fixed versions the XSD patterns require. The `SDMX.URN` check exempts these references (@sec-sdmx-identity). Both agreements are cheap and let FMR validate data under a provision agreement later.

## Global alignment {#sec-sdmx-global}

Project codes are aligned to global code values where a global list exists (D32). Alignment is by value where the project code rule allows, and otherwise by the `global_urn` column, which becomes the `GLOBAL_CODE` annotation. The global lists cannot be referenced or extended: they carry legacy, non-semver versions, and a semver artefact may not reference a legacy-versioned one (@sec-sdmx-identity).

| Project list | Global list (version) | Alignment |
|---|---|---|
| `CL_FREQ` | `SDMX:CL_FREQ(2.1)` | `A`; `global_urn` |
| `CL_SEX` | `SDMX:CL_SEX(2.1)` | `F` and `M` already match; `global_urn` |
| `CL_AGE` | `IAEG-SDGs:CL_AGE(1.25)` | `Y_LT15` is renamed `Y0T14`; `Y15T24`, `Y25T64` and `Y_GE65` already match. All four get a `global_urn`. No data row uses an age band today, so no data changes. |
| `CL_URBANISATION` | `IAEG-SDGs:CL_URBANISATION(1.10)` | `U` and `R` match and get a `global_urn`. `CAP` and `OU` stay as project children of `U`, with `global_urn` empty; `CAP` is not the global `CITY`. `SDMX:CL_DEG_URB(1.0)` is not used, because its codes `URB` and `RUR` would force renames. |
| `CL_OBS_STATUS` | `SDMX:CL_OBS_STATUS(2.3)` | `A`, `E`, `M`, `O`, `U`, `D` and `Q` all exist. `name_en` takes the global names exactly; the project's more specific wording stays in `definition_en`. `global_urn` on all seven. |
| `CL_UNIT_MEASURE` (renamed from `CL_UNIT`) | `IAEG-SDGs:CL_UNIT_MEASURE(1.20)` | `HA` to `HA`, `INDEX` to `IX`, `LCU` to `CUR_LCU`, `COUNT` to `NUMBER`. `PPP_USD` stays unaligned. `SHARE` (0 to 1), `PERSON`, `HH`, `HE`, `TLU`, `DAY` and `YEAR` have no equivalent. The global list has no ISO 4217 codes, so every code in `CL_AREA.currency` (today `XOF`) is added with `global_urn` empty; `LCU` stays as the currency-neutral unit. |
| `CL_AREA` | `WB:CL_REF_AREA_WDI(1.0)` | ISO3 ids already match; `global_urn` for `SEN` and `GNB`. This list is published by the World Bank DDP service, not by the Global Registry. |
| `CL_COMP_BREAKDOWN`, `QUINT_*` | `IAEG-SDGs:CL_QUANTILE(1.1)` | Ids keep the project prefix (@sec-code-rules); `global_urn` to `Q1` to `Q5`. |
| all others | none found | `global_urn` empty |

: Alignment of project codelists to global lists (D32) {#tbl-sdmx-global}

Every `global_urn` is a full code URN. The alignment was fetched once and committed as `pipeline/migrations/0.3.0/inputs/ALIGNMENT.csv`; the migration reads that table and makes no network call.

## What stays outside SDMX {#sec-sdmx-outside}

Project-only metadata stays CSV and is documented as tooling metadata outside SDMX (D45): `TAB_PLAN.csv`, `SERIES_PLAN.csv` (beyond what `CL_SERIES` carries), `RULES.csv`, `INDICATOR_QUALIFIERS.csv`, `QUALIFIER_PAIRS.csv`, the `LEGACY_*` files, `COLUMNS.csv`, `DSD_AFW360_HH.csv` itself and the manifests. SDMX cannot express required coverage or arithmetic rules, so the project validator keeps that job. This release has no VTL and no DataConstraint. A DataConstraint for allowed content is a later option.

## The generated `sdmx/` folder {#sec-sdmx-generated}

`pipeline/build_sdmx.R` reads `metadata/` and `content/` and writes `sdmx/`:

```
sdmx/
  README.md                            what is here, how it is generated, how to load it into FMR
  structures/AFW360_structures.xml     one SDMX-ML 3.1 structure message with every artefact
  metadata/MDS_SURVEYS.csv             SDMX-CSV 2.1 metadata messages (D43)
  metadata/MDS_SOURCES.csv
  metadata/MDS_TEXT.csv
  metadata/MDS_FIGURES.csv
```

```
Rscript pipeline/build_sdmx.R --root .           # rewrite sdmx/
Rscript pipeline/build_sdmx.R --root . --check   # exit 1 if any file under sdmx/ is stale
```

**Staleness rule.** The files under `sdmx/` are committed with the metadata that produced them. A pull request that changes `metadata/` or `content/` without regenerating `sdmx/` fails the check, in the same way as a stale table of this document (D28, D20). Nobody edits `sdmx/` by hand.

Three validator checks cover the structure message:

- `SDMX.XSD`: the message is valid against the SDMX-ML 3.1 XSDs vendored in `pipeline/xsd/sdmx-ml-3.1/`.
- `SDMX.URN`: every URN referenced inside the message resolves to an artefact in the same message, every `Parent` exists, every sub-agency is declared, and every reference from a semver artefact points at a semver artefact, except the `(1.0)` organisation-scheme items.
- `SDMX.IDENT`: every maintainable has `agencyID` `WB.AFW360` (`WB` for `AGENCIES`), a version of the form `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` (absent on the three fixed-version schemes), an id valid for the XSD, and an English name.

`tools/verify/` is an independent reader in Python (pysdmx), used by reviewers and never by the pipeline (D30). `pipeline/import_sdmx.R` does the reverse of the generator: it reads an SDMX-ML structure message and shows (`--diff`) or writes (`--apply`) the changes to the CSVs under `metadata/`.

## Editing and validating with FMR {#sec-sdmx-fmr}

The Fusion Metadata Registry (FMR) can load the structure message, validate data files against it, and edit artefacts. It is optional: everything is published as plain files in the repository, and no live registry or REST service is run for the dashboard (D36). FMR is installed without Docker, as Apache Tomcat 10.1 with the FMR 12 WAR on Java 21 and a database. If the install is blocked, FMR is a later step and the files are kept FMR-loadable (D35). A planned page, `fmr-guide.qmd`, will give the exact steps. The workflow is:

1. `Rscript pipeline/build_sdmx.R --root .` generates `sdmx/`.
2. Load `sdmx/structures/AFW360_structures.xml` into FMR.
3. Validate each data file in FMR and keep the report. Steps 1 to 3 are all that validation-only use needs.
4. To edit, work in FMR on a copy versioned `<next>-draft` and export the structure message. Run `Rscript pipeline/import_sdmx.R --diff <export.xml>` to see the changes against the CSVs, then `--apply`, and commit through a pull request. At release, bump `VERSION`, regenerate `sdmx/` and reload (@sec-change-control).

FMR 12.4 documents SDMX-ML up to 3.0 and SDMX-CSV up to 2.0. If FMR rejects the 3.1 namespaces, the generator can write the same artefacts as SDMX-ML 3.0 into `tmp/` for loading, without the MSD, the metadataflow and the metadata provision agreement. The 3.1 file stays the canonical committed output. The data files need no change, because they use no feature new in SDMX-CSV 2.1.

# Breakdowns {#sec-breakdowns}

Read this before adding a new way of splitting the population.

A **breakdown variable** classifies units: sex of household head, consumption quintile, sector of employment, poverty status. It is one row in `CL_BRK_VAR`. Its categories are rows in `CL_COMP_BREAKDOWN`, and each category code begins with its variable code.

Adding one changes no structure. It takes a row in `CL_BRK_VAR`, a row per category in `CL_COMP_BREAKDOWN`, and a line in `TAB_PLAN`.

## Initial breakdown variables {#sec-initial-breakdowns}

@tbl-brk-vars lists the registered breakdown variables with their categories. It is generated from `CL_BRK_VAR.csv` and `CL_COMP_BREAKDOWN.csv`. A variable whose universe reads `TBD` is registered from a legacy label whose population the producer has not yet confirmed; it stays `DRAFT` until then.

{{< include generated/tbl-brk-vars.md >}}

`slot_order` values are spaced by 10 so that new variables can go in between, as `DEC_MKT` (15) and `EMP_STATUS` (55) already do. **`slot_order` is immutable once the variable is `ACTIVE`**: the key of every crossed row depends on it, so changing it would change the identity of existing observations.

`DEC_MKT` is registered for fiscal-incidence work, where households are ranked by market income; `QUINT` ranks them by consumption per capita. Two different rankings are two different variables, and each states its basis in `definition_en`.

## Every breakdown variable carries a universe {#sec-universe}

`CL_BRK_VAR.universe` names the population that the categories partition. This is what makes each of `POP_SH`, `POP_HH_SH` and `POP_HE_SH` work as a single indicator for its `stat_unit`: the share is the category's weighted count divided by the universe's, and the row's `N_POP` is the universe's (@sec-values). "Share of employed in agriculture" (individuals, `POP_SH`) and "share of households with two enterprises" (households, `POP_HH_SH`) use the same mechanism but different codes, because they count different units (D4).

A recall period that defines who belongs to a group — "employed in the last 12 months" versus "employed right now" — is a property of that group's universe, not of the share indicator. It is recorded in `CL_BRK_VAR.universe` and the category's `definition_en`, never by giving the indicator a different `ref_period`. `POP_SH`, `POP_HH_SH` and `POP_HE_SH` all carry `ref_period = INTERVIEW`, whatever recall period their breakdown's universe uses.

## Worked example: adding sector of employment {#sec-example-sector}

1. Decide whose characteristic it is. "Sector of an individual's main job" (`EMP_SECTOR`, describes `IND`) and "sector of the household head's main job" (`HHH_SECTOR`, describes `HHH`) are two different variables. The first can break down only individual-level indicators; the second can break down household indicators such as the poverty rate.
2. Register it in `CL_BRK_VAR`: `describes = IND`, `applies_to_units = IND`, `universe = employed persons aged 15–64`, `classification = ISIC Rev.4`, `partition = Y`, `slot_order = 60`.
3. Register the categories in `CL_COMP_BREAKDOWN`: `EMP_SECTOR_AGR` for ISIC section A, `EMP_SECTOR_IND` for B–F and `EMP_SECTOR_SER` for G–U.
4. Add a cut to `TAB_PLAN`.
5. Produce the rows. When the cut is crossed with individual sex, the rows for women also carry `SEX=F`. When it is crossed with quintile, `QUINT` has the lower `slot_order`, so it takes slot 1 and `EMP_SECTOR` takes slot 2.

# Qualifiers {#sec-qualifiers}

Read this before adding a poverty line, a PPP round, a welfare concept or any other variant of an existing measure.

A **qualifier variable** changes what is measured for the same units. It is one row in `CL_QUAL_VAR`, and its categories are rows in `CL_QUALIFIER`. Adding one is a codelist change, not a structural one (@sec-add-qualifier). @tbl-qual-vars lists the registered variables with their categories; it is generated from `CL_QUAL_VAR.csv` and `CL_QUALIFIER.csv`. `slot_order` is immutable once a variable is `ACTIVE`, for the same reason as a breakdown's.

{{< include generated/tbl-qual-vars.md >}}

## Poverty lines {#sec-povlines}

@tbl-povlines is generated from the `POVLINE` rows of `CL_QUALIFIER.csv` and the pairings in `QUALIFIER_PAIRS.csv`.

{{< include generated/tbl-povlines.md >}}

\$2.15, \$3.65 and \$6.85 are the international, lower-middle-income and upper-middle-income lines at 2017 PPP; \$3.00, \$4.20 and \$8.30 are their 2021 PPP replacements. `POVLINE_NPL` means "the national line of this survey", whose value differs by country and round.

## PPP beyond poverty {#sec-ppp}

The `PPP` qualifier also marks values expressed in PPP dollars, such as mean consumption per capita per day in 2021 PPP dollars. Values in local currency carry no `PPP` code (`_Z`); their currency comes from `CL_AREA`.

# Metadata files {#sec-metadata}

This section is the reference for every CSV under `metadata/` and `content/`: what each file holds and which columns must be filled. Most of them are *codelists* (`CL_*`). A codelist is the list of valid codes for one column of the data file, with the meaning of each code. The rest are *relations* between codes (which qualifiers an indicator takes, which categories pair), *rules* the values must satisfy, *registries* (surveys, sources, boundaries, figures) and the *plans* of which cuts and series to produce.

The column tables in this section are generated from `metadata/structure/COLUMNS.csv`, the registry of every file's columns, and the code tables from the codelists themselves (@sec-generated-tables).

Rules for every CSV under `metadata/` and `content/`:

- UTF-8, comma-separated, one header row. Readers must open with `utf-8-sig`, because Excel's "CSV UTF-8" writes a byte-order mark.
- Multi-valued fields are space-separated.
- No literal newlines inside a cell. Anything that needs paragraphs goes in a Markdown file (@sec-text).
- Column status: **R** required, **C** required when relevant, **O** optional.
- **Every codelist has these columns**, plus the extra ones listed in its own subsection: `code`, `name_en`, `definition_en`, `status` (`DRAFT`, `ACTIVE`, `DEPRECATED`), `version_added`, `replaced_by` (C), `notes` (O).

## Code rules {#sec-code-rules}

- Uppercase ASCII letters, digits and `_`; start with a letter; at most **32 characters**, the Stata variable-name limit. P-codes are used as issued and already comply.
- `_T` and `_Z` are reserved sentinels and never appear as codes in a codelist CSV. The SDMX generator adds them as real codes, "Total" and "Not applicable", to every codelist whose dimension admits them, as the `sentinel` column of `DSD_AFW360_HH.csv` says, each with the annotation `AFW_SENTINEL` = `Y`. The importer strips them again (D42, @sec-sdmx-mapping).
- **A code never changes meaning, and is never reused or deleted.** A changed definition means a new code, with the old one `DEPRECATED` and `replaced_by` filled. Rewording a label is free.
- Breakdown and qualifier categories are `<var_code>_<category>`. The whole code must still fit in 32 characters, so keep `var_code` short.
- Indicator codes are `<THEME>_<SUBJECT>[_<DETAIL>]` and contain no poverty line, PPP round, welfare concept, COICOP division, unit or breakdown, because all of those are dimensions. Use `POV_HC`, never `POV_HC_PL420`.
- **Series ids** are the indicator code, then its qualifier categories in slot order, then its defining category, joined by `.`: `POV_HC.POVLINE_PL420.PPP_2021`, `CONS_SH.COICOP_CP01`, `POP_SH.EMP_SECTOR_AGR`. The `.` is the only place a dot appears in any code. A series id is immutable once the series is `ACTIVE` (D13).
- **Source ids** follow the code rules and are unique in `SOURCES.csv`, with one exception: they end in a run-version suffix `_v<N>`, whose lowercase `v` is the only lowercase letter allowed in any code. The recommended pattern is `<ISO3>_<SURVEY>_<PROGRAM>_v<N>`, for example `SEN_EHCVM2021_LEGACY_v1`.
- In Stata, name the variable holding an indicator after its code in lower case, so no lookup table is needed.
- **Codes are also SDMX ids.** Every code becomes an SDMX code id, which may hold only letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `@` and `$`. The rules above are stricter, except for the `.` in series ids (open decision 12). Artefact ids such as `CL_SEX` or `DSD_AFW360_HH` are NCNames: a letter, then letters, digits, `_` or `-` (@sec-sdmx-identity).
- **Codes follow global lists where one exists** (D32). A code that matches a global code keeps or takes that code's value where these rules allow, and records the global code's full URN in `global_urn` (@sec-sdmx-global).

## `CL_INDICATOR.csv`: the indicator dictionary {#sec-cl-indicator}

Beyond the common columns, the dictionary has the columns in @tbl-cl-indicator. The dictionary describes **what an indicator is**: its population (`stat_unit`, `universe_unit`, `universe_filter`, `numerator`, `weight`), its statistic and reference period, its unit (`unit_measure`, with `unit_denom`, `unit_time`, `price_basis` and `price_ref_year` for levels and money), its plausible range, how the dashboard shows it (`display_as`, `decimals`, `higher_is`, `short_name_en`), its provenance in the microdata (`source_questionnaire`, `source_vars`, `program`) and its owner. Which qualifiers it takes is in `INDICATOR_QUALIFIERS.csv` (@sec-relations), and which rules its values must satisfy is in `RULES.csv` (@sec-rules); neither is a column of the dictionary any more (D18).

{{< include generated/tbl-cl-indicator.md >}}

`ref_period` is an ISO 8601 duration (`P7D`, `P12M`, `P3Y`) or `INTERVIEW`; write `P12M`, never `P1Y`. `unit_measure` for money is always the placeholder `LCU`; the data row resolves it to the country's currency (@sec-values).

`display_as` fixes a defect the dashboard has today, where every value is formatted as a percentage. A share stored as 0.37 displays as `37.0%`, and `POV_NUM` stored as 6520000 displays as `6.52` (millions).

**Why the population fields matter.** `HHH_SEX_F` means "people living in female-headed households" for a person-level poverty rate, and "enterprises in female-headed households" for an enterprise indicator. Without `stat_unit`, `universe_*` and `weight`, person-weighted and household-weighted numbers end up on the same chart. `statistic` matters too: a budget share can be the mean of household shares (`MEAN`) or the share of aggregate spending (`RATIO_TOTALS`), and the two differ.

## `CL_BRK_VAR.csv` {#sec-cl-brk-var}

Beyond the common columns (`code` is the `var_code`), the file has the columns in @tbl-cl-brk-var. `describes` says whose characteristic the variable is (`IND`, `HHH` for the household head, `HH`, `HE`); `applies_to_units` lists the `stat_unit` values it may break down; `universe` names the population its categories partition (@sec-universe); `partition` is `Y` when the categories are mutually exclusive and exhaustive; `requires_qual` lists qualifier variables the categories depend on, such as `POVLINE PPP` for `POOR`; `slot_order` fixes the slot the variable takes in a crossed row.

{{< include generated/tbl-cl-brk-var.md >}}

## `CL_COMP_BREAKDOWN.csv` {#sec-cl-comp-breakdown}

Extra columns: `var_code` (R), `parent` (O, a category of the same variable, for nested classifications), `order` (R, display order). `definition_en` is required wherever the boundary is not obvious, such as age cutoffs, ISIC groupings and quantile ranking rules.

A category's variable is always looked up through this `var_code` column, never inferred by parsing the code's prefix: `HE_` is a prefix of `HE_COUNT_0`, but that does not make it a category of a variable called `HE`.

## `CL_QUAL_VAR.csv` and `CL_QUALIFIER.csv` {#sec-cl-qual}

`CL_QUAL_VAR` extra columns: `slot_order` (R), `requires` (C, other qualifier variables that must appear with it, such as `PPP` for `POVLINE`), `owner` (R).

`CL_QUALIFIER` extra columns: `var_code` (R), `value` (C, the numeric parameter, such as 3.00 for `POVLINE_PL300`), `basis` (C, what that value is expressed in), `order` (R).

Which categories of one qualifier variable may appear with which categories of another is not a column of either codelist; it is a row of `QUALIFIER_PAIRS.csv` (@sec-relations, D18). When a category's allowed set for some qualifier variable is `_Z` — as `POVLINE_NPL`'s is for `PPP` — that overrides the variable-level `requires`: a national-line row does not also require a PPP round, even though `POVLINE` otherwise requires `PPP`.

## `CL_GEO_SCHEME.csv` and `CL_GEO.csv` {#sec-cl-geo}

**Schemes are parallel, not nested.** ADM1 regions, ADM2 départements, Senegal's zones and Guinea-Bissau's agro-ecological zones are four different ways of cutting a country, and each is stored as its own set of units. Even where one scheme happens to group the units of another, as Senegal's zones group its regions, nothing is derived from that nesting, and no scheme is required to decompose into another.

`CL_GEO_SCHEME` has one row per country and scheme, keyed `ref_area` + `code` (@tbl-cl-geo-scheme). `has_geometry` is `Y` only for `ADM0` and `ADM1` (@sec-maps-scope). `nests_in` names another scheme only where nesting is genuine, for optional roll-up checks, never to derive geometry.

{{< include generated/tbl-cl-geo-scheme.md >}}

`CL_GEO` has one row per spatial unit (@tbl-cl-geo). Codes are P-codes for admin units (`SN03`, `GW08`) and `<ISO2>_<SCHEME><nn>` for other schemes (`SN_ZONES01`). `valid_from` and `valid_to` describe the **boundary vintage** the code belongs to, not the validity of the data; `valid_to` is empty while current.

{{< include generated/tbl-cl-geo.md >}}

The shapefiles in `data_raw/shp/` already carry these P-codes: `SN01` is Dakar, `SN03` is Fatick, and `GW08` is Bissau (the current tables call it `SAB`). Maps join on codes, never on names.

`name_en` "as issued by the boundary source" fits `ADM0` and `ADM1`, but not zones or agro-ecological zones, which have no such source. For those schemes `name_en` is `TBD` until confirmed with the producer, and the boundary-sourced rule does not apply to them.

## `CL_AREA.csv` {#sec-cl-area}

Extra columns: `iso2` (R, the P-code prefix), `currency` (R, ISO 4217), `wb_region` (R).

Currency matters more than it seems. "FCFA" is two different currencies: `XOF` (CFA franc BCEAO, used in WAEMU, including SEN and GNB) and `XAF` (CFA franc BEAC). Eight AFW economies use neither. Monetary values in `LCU` are therefore **not comparable across countries**; comparison needs a PPP-denominated indicator.

## Small codelists {#sec-small-codelists}

@tbl-small-codelists is generated from the codelist files themselves. `_T` and `_Z` are valid in `SEX` and `AGE` in addition to the listed codes (@sec-sentinels). `CL_URBANISATION` has a `parent` column: `CAP` and `OU` are children of `U`. The parent `U` is not itself produced by the current plan; a reader who wants urban as a whole aggregates `CAP` and `OU` by `N_POP`, which a legacy file cannot supply.

{{< include generated/tbl-small-codelists.md >}}

`CL_STATISTIC` also carries `admits_se` (R): `Y` when a value computed with this statistic can carry a standard error and confidence interval (as `PROPORTION` and `MEAN` do), `N` when it cannot; @tbl-columns' `STD_ERR` / `CI_LOWER` / `CI_UPPER` requirement reads this column. `CL_UNIT` holds the units of the dictionary; a data row's `UNIT_MEASURE` is one of them or, for money, an ISO 4217 code registered as some country's `currency` in `CL_AREA`.

## `SURVEYS.csv` {#sec-surveys}

One row per country and survey round (@tbl-surveys). `status` is `DRAFT` until a producer confirms the record and `ACTIVE` once confirmed, the same convention as a codelist's. `representative_levels` is **advisory metadata** that the dashboard may display; it does not gate publication. `analysis_units` says which file each `stat_unit` is estimated from, so `N_OBS` is interpretable. Senegal's row is the worked example: EHCVM 2021, fieldwork 2021-11 to 2022-09, national line 519.8 XOF per capita per day; the source says the line was "estimated using the EHCVM 2018 … in current prices", so its price year is an inference and is recorded as one in `notes`.

{{< include generated/tbl-surveys.md >}}

## Manifest {#sec-manifest}

`AFW360_HH_<ISO3>_<YEAR>_<ESTIMATION>_manifest.csv` has two columns, `key` and `value`. The keys are:

`structure_id` (`WB.AFW360:AFW360_HH(0.3.0)`; equals every row's `STRUCTURE_ID`), `sdmx_csv_version` (`2.1.0`), `dsd_version`, `metadata_version`, `ref_area`, `time_period`, `estimation` (`CL_ESTIMATION`; equals every row's `ESTIMATION`), `survey_id` (the base survey, also for a model-based file), `sources` (the `SOURCE_ID` values that appear in the file, space-separated), `file_name`, `n_rows`, `producer`, `program`, `software`, `run_timestamp` (ISO 8601), `status` (`DRAFT`, `SUBMITTED`, `VALIDATED`, `PUBLISHED`), `notes`.

The manifest summarises the file; it holds nothing that a row needs. Precision is on each row (`PRECISION`), and the program run that produced each row is its `SOURCE_ID`, whose registry row carries the program version and inputs (@sec-sources). The `source_type` and `precision` keys of version 0.1.0 are gone (D15, D16, D17).

`dsd_version` is not chosen independently: the DSD is versioned with the metadata package, so it equals `metadata/VERSION`.

In version 0.3.0 the key `dataflow` became `structure_id`, the SDMX short reference to the dataflow and its version, and `sdmx_csv_version` was added (D46). The other 15 keys are unchanged. The manifest is a project-level sidecar, not an SDMX artefact: it describes a file (D43, D45).

`TIME_PERIOD` is the year the estimate refers to, which is **not** always a survey year. A microsimulated 2026 poverty rate has `TIME_PERIOD=2026`, `ESTIMATION=MODEL`, a source whose `survey_id` is `SEN_EHCVM_2021`, and `OBS_STATUS=E` on every row (@sec-estimation-method).

## `TAB_PLAN.csv`: which cuts are produced {#sec-tab-plan}

A *cut* is one way of splitting the population, such as by residence, by region or by quintile. A row that lists two breakdowns is a crossed cut, such as quintile by sex of household head. `TAB_PLAN` is what turns the dictionary into a list of required rows (@sec-required-rows).

There is one row per cut, with the columns in @tbl-tab-plan. They give the codes used, not yes/no flags: `geo_scheme` is `_T` or a scheme code, `urbanisation` is `_T` or a set such as `CAP OU R`, `sex` and `age` are `_T` or sets of codes, `comp_breakdowns` lists breakdown variable codes in slot order, and `themes` is `ALL` or a list of theme codes.

{{< include generated/tbl-tab-plan.md >}}

The current plan (@tbl-initial-plan) reproduces the legacy Excel tables. The zone cut needs one row per country, because the two countries' zone schemes differ. Share series add their defining breakdown to every cut they are produced for, which is why the data files hold crossed rows, such as sector of employment within quintile, that no single plan row names.

{{< include generated/tbl-initial-plan.md >}}

## `SERIES_PLAN.csv` {#sec-series-plan}

`plans/SERIES_PLAN.csv` is the explicit list of series to produce (@sec-required-rows), with the columns in @tbl-series-plan. A series is one row: its `series_id` (@sec-code-rules), the `INDICATOR`, the qualifier categories in `MEASURE_QUALS`, and, for a share indicator, the category it is a share of in `DEFINING_BREAKDOWN`, for example `EMP_SECTOR_AGR` for the series "share of employed persons working in agriculture".

{{< include generated/tbl-series-plan.md >}}

Three columns were added in version 0.2.0:

- **`name_en`** is the display name of the series, what a chart title or a report sentence says (D13). It is composed by default from the indicator's `short_name_en` and the qualifier and category names, and a human overwrites it wherever the composed form reads badly. The dashboard shows `name_en`, never the id.
- **`estimation`** lists the file kinds in which the series is expected: `SURVEY`, `MODEL`, or both space-separated (D17). Every series of version 0.1.0 has `SURVEY`.
- **`status`** gains two values beyond `DRAFT` and `ACTIVE` (D23). On a row for a specific country, `NOT_PRODUCED` records that the country's survey cannot support the series, and `DEVIATES` records that the country produces it under a definition that departs from the dictionary's; both require `notes`. A country row overrides the `ALL` row for the same `series_id` (@sec-required-rows).

## Verification rules: `RULES.csv` {#sec-rules}

Every rule that the validator applies to values is a row of `metadata/rules/RULES.csv` (D18). Rules used to be space-separated tokens in a column of the indicator dictionary; as a table they can be versioned, given a severity and a tolerance, and attached to a series rather than an indicator, without touching the dictionary.

{{< include generated/tbl-rules.md >}}
